Study area: All 30 districts of the state of Odisha, where farmers have received recommendations for at least one season through two channels of dissemination, CSC and/or PxD, were selected for this study.

In the similar format, six districts were selected from PxD and seven from the CSC channel. From each district, 25 farmers were randomly selected from each channel. In total, 325 farmers were selected for the study: 175 farmers from CSC and 150 from the PxD channel of recommendation dissemination ( Table 2 ).

This study evaluates the effectiveness of in-person and telephonic dissemination pathways for Rice Crop Manager (RCM) in Odisha, India and their influence on farmers’ adoption. Two dissemination channels were evaluated: (1) face-to-face delivery through Common Service Centres (CSC), where farmers received printed advisories; and (2) telephonic dissemination facilitated by Precision Development (PxD), which provided advisories over voice calls at the beginning of the season followed by periodic advisory calls and reminders. Using semi-structured questionnaires, researchers interviewed farmers at the end of one cropping season, after advisories were provided at the onset. Key emphasis lies on user feedback about the RCM recommendations’ utility in crop management and the influence of dissemination modes on adoption decisions.

excerpts: National Cyclone Risk Mitigation Project (NCRMP) was drawn up to strengthen the structural and non-structural mitigation efforts towards reducing the risk and vulnerability of the coastal districts to cyclone-related disasters.
The project was divided into four components, namely :
**Component-A:-** Early Warning Dissemination System (EWDS)-Last Mile Connectivity
**Component-B:-** Construction of Cyclone Risk Mitigation Infrastructure like Multipurpose Cyclone Shelters (MCS), Approach Roads, Saline Embankments, Shelter level equipment

**Component-C:-** Shelter level capacity building (Technical assistance for capacity building on hazard risk management by **NDMA and National Institute of Disaster Management (NIDM) and** the shelter level capacity building activities were carried out by OSDMA)
**Component-D:-** Implementation Assistance (Project Management and Monitoring applicable to all implementing agencies )
The total financial outlay of the project was of Rs.653.79 crore which was later revised to Rs. 695.97 crores with earmarked fund for component A, B, C & D.
Components A, C and D are fully funded by the Central Government.
However, Component-B (Rs. 586.72 crore) is being funded by the Centre and the State on the ratio 75:25.

The Project is being implemented in 22 blocks under 6 coastal districts (Balasore, Bhadrak, Jagatsinghpur, Kendrapara, Puri & Ganjam) with a view to establishing a fool-proof communication system to address the existing gap of disseminating disaster warning up to the community level.
